judged: W1-MAP-DEFECTS — the reachability fix (map moved to second in WALK_ORDER) and the fog-of-war removal (AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-02)

score.aggregation: min-over-axes, per Ruling W2 — no averaging away a failing axis

the_gap_the_builder_named_and_i_closed.question: can a player reach the map on a phone, and is four taps on unlabelled pictograms acceptable?
the_gap_the_builder_named_and_i_closed.answer: The route exists and is four taps: drawer -> menu -> drawer -> swap_right. Every link is now evidenced. Link 3 is game/src/input/touch.js:255 (`if (hit.fromDrawer) this.drawerOpen = false;`) — the drawer shuts after EVERY petal tap, so a phone pays two taps per page-turn. Link 4 is the shipped ring: swap_right from `inventory` lands on `map`.
the_gap_the_builder_named_and_i_closed.ruling_on_acceptability: NOT acceptable as the only route, and I am ruling rather than asking. The desktop fix was justified because the map was four presses away with nothing announcing that the pages turn. On a phone the map is four TAPS away on pictograms with no text at all — the same argument with more force. It is not the blocker, because the map is at least on the forward tap-walk. The journal is not, and that is the blocker.
the_gap_the_builder_named_and_i_closed.reversible: Yes. What would overturn it: a touch run in which a person who was told nothing reaches the map, or a labelled drawer that names the pages.

biggest_gap.what: `map` was placed immediately before `journal` in UISystem.WALK_ORDER. `map`'s own navigable ring excludes `journal` (NEVER_ADJACENT, enforcing RI-UIX04 Q7), so the forward page-walk steps over the journal and never returns: inventory -> map -> sheet -> spells -> wait -> (closes). Before the fix the same walk reached all five peer screens and hit the journal on press one. swap_left from `inventory` lands on `world` and CLOSES the menu, so the reversal that would reach it is not something a player finds by accident.
biggest_gap.numbers: desktop page-turns from the inventory: map 4 -> 1; journal 1 -> 3 with a direction reversal, and OFF the forward walk. Phone taps: map 10 -> 4; journal 4 -> 8.
biggest_gap.remedy: One word. `['world','inventory','map','sheet','journal','spells','wait','levelup']` — measured: forward walk becomes inventory -> map -> sheet -> journal -> spells -> wait, nothing skipped, map still one turn away. The structural rule belongs in a comment beside the constant: any two screens in NEVER_ADJACENT must not be neighbours in WALK_ORDER, because the ring is filtered per-mode and an excluded neighbour is stepped OVER, not stopped at.
biggest_gap.acceptance: node corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/w1-map-defects/walk-reachability.mjs exits 0 with `SKIPPED by the forward walk: nothing`, and map=1 still.

what_held_up: The fog removal is a correction, not a preference, and I verified the reading verbatim. RI-WLD06 §5 bans 'fog-of-war reveal-on-approach' and permits the surface as 'paper, static, hand-drawn'. The builder was right and the corpus was on the owner's side.

The boundary is where the corpus puts it. roads.json is not imported by the map screen; roads_drawn and routes_drawn are declared 0. 'The map may show the world, it may not show the way' is a fair statement of S35 as it survives.

Both control arms are real and both are convincing to a person, not just to a number. Delete-the-fix is the black rectangle the owner saw; the null control is a whole province carrying 34 unearned squares under the foot line 'Places I have stood in.'

All three sabotage anchors occur EXACTLY ONCE at HEAD, and I watched each guard throw on a perturbed copy rather than trusting that it would (corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/w1-map-defects/anchor-audit.mjs, exit 0).
RI-UIX04 Q7 holds in both directions in the shipped ring: the map's ring has no journal, the journal's ring has no map.
what_did_not_hold_up: THE HEAD ARM IS NOT IN THE LANDED FOG RECORD. reports/w1-map-defects/fog-control.json holds only `deletefix` and `markers`; the two checks that measure HEAD are absent, so its `pass: true` was computed without the experiment's positive arm. Its run started at 14:34:40 and fog-head.png was written at 14:34:19 — twenty-one seconds EARLIER, from a previous run.

THE SOURCE CHANGED MID-EXPERIMENT. fog-deletefix.png (14:37:32) is headed 'Where I have been'; fog-markers.png (14:41:21) is headed 'The Province'. game/src/ui/screens/map.js was edited between two arms of the same run. Cell counts are unaffected (the heading is a literal outside the draw loop) and the conclusion is not in doubt, but the arms were not run against one source. Visible in the stacked artifact, which is why I stacked them.

map-probe S8 AND S12 ARE TAUTOLOGIES AT HEAD. Both assert drawn_cells === cells_in_view, and in screens/map.js the two counters increment on ADJACENT LINES with nothing between them — the comment says 'They are equal by construction now'. Only a gate spliced between the two increments can break it, which is exactly and only the deletefix shape. A gate placed one line earlier hides any fraction of the province and both stay green. The check with teeth is drawn_cells === total_cells (42,846) in the province view; one line each.

ARBITRATION.md WAS NOT UPDATED. S35 still reads 'Undiscovered is not merely unlabelled, it is unrendered' as live binding text with no pointer to the amendment that struck it, and S38(b) — 'no square and no revealed cell may exist that the asserted footprint does not imply' — is now literally false of the drawn map. The substance is fine: the owner's 2026-08-14 instruction is a later owner ruling and outranks. The record is not: S35's own row models the missing signpost ('AMENDED wave 1 by S38 — READ THAT ROW BEFORE ENFORCING THIS ONE') for the very same clause, and the W1-MAP-r2 critic has already been caught out once by grepping ARBITRATION.md and missing an amendment. Remediation is one seam row, no code.

Every failing check in this verdict comes from enumerating the SHIPPED module in bare Node, where frame starvation cannot reach. The one live observation I made (eleven touch controls on the glass with no `menu`) is reported as a reproduction of the builder's observation, not as a result.
measurement_trap.contention_at_start: load 18.92 over 4 cores = 4.73 per core, 4 browser instances — OVER the 4.0 ceiling. I waited for 3.79 before launching one browser, and it climbed back to 6.6 within minutes as other agents launched theirs.
measurement_trap.proceeded_anyway: Yes, with ONE browser, and I am saying so here as HAZARDS requires. It did not pay off: see below.

referred_onward: THE PROVINCE READS AS A CHOROPLETH, NOT AS LAND. Removing the fog made the whole raster visible for the first time and what it shows is thirteen flat blocks of saturated region colour — one pure black, one bright red, one orange — where all five Morrowind plates show continuous muted shaded relief with the sea a flat field behind. The height shading IS applied and the region palette drowns it. Predates both fixes and the builder correctly scoped it out, so I did not score it; but under Ruling W1 it is wave-1 work and it is now what the owner sees when the map opens. Wants its own piece against the five plates.

REF-A12b PROVENANCE. The amendment says all five map plates are late saves that cannot settle what a fresh character sees. REF-A12b-map__mw-219518267.jpg shows a whole drawn landmass carrying exactly ONE place square — closer to a fresh character than a late save, and it supports the amendment more strongly than the amendment claims. But its header reads 'Forsaken Land', which is not a Vvardenfell, Solstheim or Mournhold region: that plate is from a mod, not vanilla Morrowind, and the corpus does not say so. Belongs to whoever owns the interface references.
